correctness.rationale: For a root in layer i, its downset contains all earlier layers and the root. The weights are zero there, one on its layer peers, and the sum of m_a for i≤a<j on layer j>i. Thus the initial cone is followed by the joins of the full first j layers; m_i≥2 separates the first two positive thresholds when both exist. The shifted tensor product of the augmented chains of the discrete layers has reduced homology free of rank M_j in degree j−1 only. The inclusion into the next join factors through the cone on any new vertex, killing reduced homology. In degree zero the class of the root splits off naturally, leaving the reduced transient part exactly as stated. For a bottom root the largest degree gives r, the first finite deaths give m_1, the subsequent finite lengths give the intervening sizes, and M_r/M_{r-1}+1 gives m_r, also for r=2. The top births strictly decrease with the layer of the root, down to 1 for the top root. In top degree the equal numbers of essential bars must match to each other, at exact cost D−1. The difference of the two pointwise weights on U_y is the difference of the counts of U_y in the two opposite downset differences, so its absolute value is bounded by the larger mutual furtherness, D for these roots. Fixing r gives (D−1)/D tending to 1 in the prescribed positive degree. This is an all-parameter proof, not a finite extrapolation.
